data_ui.chart_flag_truncated_bar_axis: Bar axis does not start at zero
data_ui.chart_teach_truncated_bar_axis: Bars show size by length. If the axis starts above zero, small gaps look huge. Start bars at zero.
data_ui.chart_flag_dual_axis: Two different axes in one chart
data_ui.chart_teach_dual_axis: Two scales can make unrelated lines look linked. Use two charts, or one shared scale.
data_ui.chart_teach_too_many_categories: Past about a dozen bars nobody can read them. Group small ones or show the top few.
data_ui.chart_teach_unsorted_bars: Sorted bars let the eye rank values at once. Sort high to low unless the order means something.
data_ui.chart_teach_missing_units: A number without a unit is a riddle. Say what is measured: units, USD, percent.
data_ui.chart_teach_smoothing_hides_spikes: A moving average can erase a spike that matters, or a typo. Look at the raw line first.
data_ui.chart_teach_pie_too_many_slices: More than about five slices cannot be compared by eye. A sorted bar chart is clearer.

glossary.trust: Trust: how much Ms. Hanh believes your reports. Good, well-sourced reports raise it; wrong, over-confident ones lower it. At zero you are fired.
glossary.energy: Energy: how many verification checks you can run today. Each paid check uses 1 Energy and half an hour. Repeat checks on the same article are free.
glossary.tier_chinh_thuc: Official: central bank, regulators and statistics offices. Usually reliable, sometimes slow.
glossary.tier_bao_chi: Press: newspapers. Fairly reliable but may exaggerate.
glossary.tier_mang_xa_hoi: Social media: fast but often rumor. Verify before you rely on it.
glossary.tier_noi_bo: Insider: colleagues and tips. Early but unconfirmed.

steps.text: This is today's question. Your job: forecast the answer using the news.
Open Browser to read the news. Colored badges show how much to trust each source.
Click a news card to select it.
Open Code Pad to verify the selected article.
Press Use. Each check costs Energy (the dots) and you only get a few a day.
Pin the articles you trust. Go back to Browser and press Pin.
Open Files: today's data export lands here. Open it and look before you trust it. Exports can repeat rows or spell names in different ways.
In Sheet, clean the table with steps, for example Dedupe. Each step shows its row count and can be undone.
In Charts, build a chart from your table and press Pin chart. Mail can attach it to your report.
Open Mail to write your report.
Pick a forecast and how confident you are. The Analysis button adds your charts and findings (optional).
Press Send. You cannot edit afterwards.

open: Open Files and open today's sales export. Look before you trust it.
Click the Files icon on the left, then press Open.
look: Scroll the table. Do rows repeat? Are names spelled the same way every time? Press Next when you have looked.
Sort a column from its header menu to bring look-alike rows together.
dedupe: Exports often repeat rows. Add a Dedupe step.
In Sheet press Dedupe, leave the key columns empty (all columns) and press OK.
standardize: A name can be spelled in several ways. Merge the spellings with the Text step.
Press Text, pick the region column, tick the odd spellings and write the right name in Into.
group: Now add up the units per region with a Group step.
Press Group: group by region, aggregate units with sum.
chart: Chart the result: a bar chart from the clean table, sorted, then Pin chart.
In Charts choose Source clean, type Bar, sort descending, then press Pin chart.
attach: Open Mail, press Analysis and attach your chart.
Mail icon, then Analysis (n), then Attach next to your chart.
finding: In the Analysis panel choose your finding. Trust the table you cleaned.
Open the finding list and pick the answer your bar chart shows.
forecast: Pick a forecast and your confidence for the market question.
Choose Up, Down or Flat, then Low, Medium or High.
send: Press Send. You cannot edit afterwards.

open: New rule from today: every report has a deadline (15:00). Open Files and open the steel index file.
Click the Files icon, then Open.
line: Look at the trend first: a line chart of value by date, then Pin chart.
Charts: Source raw, type Line, X date, Y value, then Pin chart.
attach: Attach that chart in Mail > Analysis so the picture travels with your report.
outliers: Does one value sit far from its neighbours? Flag it with the Outliers step (IQR rule), then decide: a one-off typo or a lasting move?
Sheet > Outliers: column value, method IQR, action remove. Check which row it removes.
finding: Choose your findings. A lasting step in the line is real information; do not delete it.
Open each finding list and pick what the cleaned data shows.
forecast: Pick a forecast and your confidence. A short history is a reason for care.
Choose Up, Down or Flat, then a confidence.
send: Press Send. You cannot edit afterwards.

open: Open Files and open the sign-up funnel.
Click the Files icon, then Open.
look: Check the exported_at column for each day. Do all days look complete? Press Next when you have looked.
Look at the last rows and compare their export time with the other days.
filter: Drop the day that is not complete with a Filter step on the date.
Sheet > Filter: column date, keep rows before the incomplete day.
group: Add up users per step with a Group step.
Press Group: group by step, aggregate users with sum.
chart: Chart the steps as a sorted bar chart from the clean table and pin it.
Charts: Source clean, type Bar, sort descending, Pin chart.
attach: Attach the chart in Mail > Analysis.
finding: Which step loses the most users compared with the step before it? Compare rates, not raw counts.
Divide each step by the one before it, then choose in the finding list.
forecast: Pick a forecast and your confidence.
Choose Up, Down or Flat, then a confidence.
send: Press Send. You cannot edit afterwards.

open: Open Files and open the A/B test log.
Click the Files icon, then Open.
group: Group by variant: count the users and add up the conversions.
Press Group: group by variant, first aggregate converted with sum, second with count.
rate: Add a computed column: conversions divided by users, so the groups can be compared.
Press Compute: name rate, operation div, A converted_sum, B converted_count.
finding: Compare the rates, then ask: could luck explain the gap with so few users? Choose carefully.
Work out conversions divided by users for A and for B, then judge the gap.
forecast: Pick your confidence honestly. Small samples deserve low confidence.
Choose a forecast, then a confidence that matches the evidence.
send: Press Send. You cannot edit afterwards.

open: Open Files and open the checkout file.
Click the Files icon, then Open.
group: Group by variant and device: add up visitors and orders. Compare like with like.
Press Group: group by variant and device, aggregate visitors with sum and orders with sum.
rate: Add a computed column: orders divided by visitors.
Press Compute: name rate, operation div, A orders_sum, B visitors_sum.
finding: Choose your findings. Check how the traffic was split before you trust any overall rate.
Compare A and B inside each device, then look at the share of each device.
forecast: Pick a forecast and your confidence.
Choose Up, Down or Flat, then a confidence.
send: Press Send. You cannot edit afterwards.

telemetry.title: Help improve this game?
telemetry.body: You can share anonymous play data: which days you finish, which tools you use and how your reports score. We never collect your name, email, device details or anything you type. Data stays on your computer. You can export it from Settings and send it to the developer if you want. You can turn this off and delete everything at any time. The id used to link your sessions is random and is deleted when you turn this off. This game is for players 16 and older.
telemetry.pseudonymous: The random session-linking id is pseudonymous personal data. Nothing is uploaded.
telemetry.exported: Play data exported. You can send this file yourself:
telemetry.export_failed: No play data exported. The file is empty or could not be written.
